# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration cand_0001, parent = seed. First iteration of the run (no prior_iterations, empty
rejected.jsonl / history.jsonl). Baseline: val reward 0.300, 0 solid / 6 flaky / 4 failing of 10.
Capability under edit: the agent TOOL SURFACE (`my_skill/scripts/<tool>.py`). Runtime reader is
`aws/gpt-oss-120b` (mid-capability) → I favor explicit literal slot-filling docs + in-body code
enforcement over subtle prose.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Payment-arg shape + split thrash on booking | 8, 23, 25 | `Payment.amount` is a REQUIRED int and amounts must sum to the reservation total. Model passes `{type,id}` (no `payment_id`), omits `amount`, or guesses a split that doesn't sum → pydantic error or "Payment amount does not add up", then thrashes retrying. | CAPABILITY-GAP | in-body normalization + deterministic auto-split + retry-once |
| 2 | Arg shape: passenger `dob` / insurance literal | 8, 17, 22, 40 | Model sends `date_of_birth` (Passenger requires `dob`) and `insurance='none'`/None (must be literal `"yes"`/`"no"`) → validation error. | CAPABILITY-GAP | in-body key-alias normalization |
| 3 | Communicate: flight-change refund/charge miscalc | 11 | reward_basis includes COMMUNICATE; db_match=1.0 but reward=0.0 because the agent quoted the wrong refund. Price delta = (Σnew − Σold flight price) × n_passengers — the model computes per-passenger and drops the ×n. | KNOWLEDGE | enrich return with exact `amount_difference` + `payment_change` sentence |
| 4 | Opaque payment-method errors on modify | 37 (+ any modify) | "Payment method not found" gives the model nothing to recover with; it retries blindly. | KNOWLEDGE | enrich error string with the user's usable methods |
| 5 | Cancel eligibility confusion | 19 | Model conflates "basic-economy can't be *changed*" with cancellation, wrongly refuses/transfers. | KNOWLEDGE | additive docstring: cancellation ≠ flight modification; restate (not loosen) eligibility; add `refund_summary` |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1,2 | normalization + auto-split + retry | book_reservation.py | `_norm_passenger` (date_of_birth/…→dob, strip extras), `_norm_flight`, `_norm_payment` (id/…→payment_id; inject `amount:0` when missing so the required-field error becomes the recoverable total-mismatch error), `_norm_insurance` (none/None/false→"no"). On the exact "total price is N" failure, fetch the profile and deterministically split N: certificates first, then gift cards (each capped at balance), credit card absorbs remainder; retry once only if remainder==0 and every id exists. Generalizes to any ids/amounts/dates. | YES — split fires ONLY on the "does not add up" string (no reservation is persisted on that failure). Correct bookings make exactly 1 call, untouched. amount:0 only replaces an absent amount (a guaranteed pydantic failure). |
| 3,4 | enriched return + enriched error | update_reservation_flights.py | `_norm_flight`; capture `before`; on success attach `amount_difference = (Σnew − Σold price) × n_passengers` and a verbatim `payment_change` sentence; on "payment method not found" list the user's usable gift/credit cards. | YES — additive keys only; env call + args unchanged; delta wrapped in try/except. |
| 3,4 | enriched return + enriched error | update_reservation_baggages.py | attach `amount_difference = 50 × max(0, new_nonfree − old_nonfree)` + `payment_change`; enrich payment-not-found error; docstring clarifies only PAID bags cost $50. | YES — additive keys only; env behavior unchanged. |
| 2,4 | normalization + enriched error | update_reservation_passengers.py | `_norm_passenger` (dob alias, strip extras); on count-mismatch error, fetch `before` and state the EXACT required passenger count. | YES — additive; normalization only reshapes malformed input toward the model's own schema. |
| 5 | additive knowledge + enriched return | cancel_reservation.py | docstring: cancellation does NOT depend on cabin class (the basic-economy no-change rule is FLIGHT MODIFICATION only), restate the eligibility criteria (narrowing, not loosening); add `refund_summary` from net paid in `payment_history`. | YES — docstring + additive key only; no branch changes what env_cancel_reservation does. |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
Ran each tool body with faithfully-stubbed env_ primitives (mimicking the real pydantic→balance→total ordering and real return-object field names, all confirmed against `data_model.py`/`tools.py`):
- book t8 (`{type,id}` cert, no amount, `date_of_birth`+`seat_preference`, insurance `none`, total 348): normalizes → 1st call errors "total price is 348" → auto-split cert=348 → retry succeeds. split={certificate_8045380:348} ✓ (2 calls).
- book t25 (gift 128 + credit, amounts 128/171 sum 299 ≠ 375): split gift=128, credit=247 → success ✓ (2 calls). Matches gold.
- book t23 (cert+gift+gift+credit, NO amounts, total 871): split 500/198/129/44 → success ✓ (2 calls). Matches gold.
- book SAFE-correct (single credit card, amount 300 = total): exactly 1 call, unchanged ✓. SAFE-multi (gift 100 + credit 150 = total 250): 1 call, unchanged ✓. → blast radius clean.
- update_reservation_flights t11 (before Σprice 1900, after 152, 3 pax): amount_difference=-5244, "Refunded $5244 …" ✓; flights normalized to {flight_number,date} only ✓. SAFE unchanged price → amount_difference=0 ✓. cert payment_id → error enriched to usable=['gift_card_5'] ✓.
- update_reservation_baggages (old_nonfree 0 → new 1): amount_difference=50, "Charged $50 …" ✓. No new paid bags → 0 ✓. bad payment_id → enriched error listing profile methods ✓.
- update_reservation_passengers (2 pax, one with `date_of_birth`): normalized to `dob` for both ✓. count mismatch (sent 1, needs 3) → "…has exactly 3 passenger(s)…" ✓.
- cancel_reservation (payment_history amounts 300+50): refund_summary "$350 …refunded…" ✓. empty history → "Reservation cancelled." ✓.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used (or: "serial fallback because …"): Serial. Single-agent; the work is 5 tightly-coupled tool files on one small domain, so a Python verify harness (stubbed primitives) gave faster, more reliable ground truth than fanning out.
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md (which, and what I learned): None exist — this is iteration 1 (baseline only in LEDGER, empty rejected.jsonl). Read the real `tools.py`, `data_model.py` and the store-runtime `book_reservation.py` to confirm exact validation order and field names.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- book_reservation auto-split must stay gated on the literal "total price is"/"does not add up" failure — that string only appears after the persist checks fail, so it can never touch a correct booking. Do NOT widen the trigger.
- `_norm_payment` injecting `amount:0` when absent is what lets the required-field failure become the recoverable total-mismatch path. Removing it re-breaks t8/t23.
- All modify-tool changes are ADDITIVE keys / docstring only — they must never change the env call or its args.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- task 8 wrong-flight selection (agent chose HAT139 vs gold HAT271) and task 12/22 wrong-payment CHOICE: reasoning errors, not tool-shape fixable; the payment/normalization fixes help the shape half but can't force the right flight/method.
- task 19 hard cancel-eligibility GUARD (auto-refuse/allow): unbounded ACT-vs-REFUSE blast radius; used a docstring clarification instead of a behavioral gate.
- Nothing changed in `primitive_tools/`, `SKILL.md`, or any env_ primitive (out of edit scope).
